about: English → Liraasa cases for the 2.5 translator, one or more per 2.5 ruling and per function-word family. expect is derived from the rulings (null: no listed word, the gap is reported); equivalents are other renderings the rulings allow, the patch's own wording among them; review marks an expectation for the author to confirm (review/questions_2_5.md). The translator must produce expect or an equivalent, and every rendering must pass the strict checker and back-translate to its frame.

cases.expect: Ki-kasa taivo po amora maivo ki?

cases.english: How many songs do you have?

cases.expect: Eli ka ki-nela de lira ki?

cases.review: English "are going" gives the progressive roni; the patch writes the plain present. Both are grammatical: should the translator drop roni for a present progressive?

cases.english: Do you know that I sing?
cases.expect: Taivo sabesia fime maivo lirala ki?

cases.english: Perhaps you know that I sing.
cases.expect: Taivo sabesia fime maivo lirala poye.

cases.english: The bread is on the table.
cases.expect: Li bumre ke su li tabu.

cases.review: English "a" gives baba; the patch writes the predicate noun bare. 0.8:R5 lets baba drop only in verse.

cases.expect: Maivo po ke baba mellinasan linu.
cases.review: "little child": the translator writes the adjective (mellinasan); the patch writes the diminutive linuti. Should "little" + noun prefer -ti?

cases.english: They were good, and no longer are.
cases.review: "they" → saivori (plural); the patch reads it as singular saivo.

cases.english: There is a friend in the home.
cases.expect: Miyo baba sora en li nimu.
Li bumre de pilo ka benasan.

cases.english: The song of the bird is beautiful.
cases.expect: Li lira de li lavra ka vanisan.

cases.english: One of the two will return.
cases.expect: Una de li dossa futu relnura.

cases.english: The bird sits behind the home.
cases.expect: Li lavra semnesia nazru li nimu.

cases.english: The bird sings; it is beautiful.
cases.expect: Li lavra lirala; ito ka vanisan.

cases.english: I open the door with the key.
cases.expect: Maivo lallela li dorbi yuta li kemye.

cases.english: She spoke in a musical voice.
cases.expect: Saivo po senosia en baba melosan valla.

cases.english: I sing more gently than you.
cases.expect: Maivo lirala la kasi molusan tamo taivo.

cases.english: I have more songs than you.
cases.expect: Maivo tovota kasi lirari tamo taivo.

cases.english: The song is more beautiful than the speech.
cases.expect: Li lira ka kasi vanisan tamo li seno.
Maivo po venreva kroti dossa deya.

cases.english: I make him eat the food.
cases.expect: Maivo vaku saivo sapusia li nami.

cases.review: "leave" is tevuluta by its first gloss; the patch writes pagopa (go).

cases.english: The song is written by me.
cases.expect: Li lira gome sarbisia gagu maivo.

cases.english: Change is very easy to resist.
cases.expect: Trana ka ruli levasan sidu zeldoza.
equivalents: Trana ke ruli levasan sidu zeldoza.
cases.review: ke or ka for "easy" (2.5:G93): the translator reads it as lasting (ka) and flags it; the patch writes ke.

cases.english: I gave the bread to my father.
cases.expect: Maivo po donuda li bumre ala maivo de pilo.
Maivo po venreva eli-pago kopisa lirala.

cases.english: I sing so that you dance.
If I had asked, you would have answered.
cases.expect: Si maivo po noma masuma, taivo po noma viki relsira.

cases.english: The person who sings is good.
cases.expect: Li nela raho lirala ka benasan.

cases.english: The sage who studies this did not see the word.
cases.expect: Li sabeyo raho lemula eli, po ne vimova li seno.
equivalents: Li sabeyo raho vismava eli, ne yehu vimova li vordu.
cases.review: word choice: study → lemula (learn) by gloss, word → seno; the patch uses vismava, vordu and the evidential yehu.

cases.english: I sing, so that perhaps you will dance.
cases.expect: Maivo lirala, kopisa taivo nosi rilura.

cases.english: I know that you might sing.
cases.expect: Maivo sabesia fime taivo nosi lirala.

cases.english: Are you so brave that you would kiss me?
cases.expect: Taivo ka tonsi corvisan fime taivo viki savalisia maivo ki?
equivalents: Taivo ke tonsi corvisan fime taivo viki savalisia maivo ki?
cases.review: ke or ka for "brave" (2.5:G93); the patch writes ke.

cases.english: As soon as you came, I sang.
cases.expect: Kureli taivo venreva, maivo po lirala.
Maivo po masuma ki-oro taivo relnura.

cases.review: "they" for one named person → saivori; the patch writes saivo.

cases.english: As for the bread, Kipo baked it.
cases.expect: Li bumre hozi, Kipo po bumreba ito.

cases.english: The singer whose song I love is here.
cases.expect: Li lirayo raho maivo amora saivo de lira, ke eli-pago.
Li krono raho maivo po lirala en ito.
Li pago raho maivo po venreva da ito.

cases.english: I don't know where you will go.
cases.expect: Maivo ne sabesia ki-pago taivo futu pagopa.

cases.review: No listed word: revo-sabesia means "recognize" in a canonical example, but its gloss is not in the data. The translator reports the gap instead of guessing; add the meaning to the curated metaphor and it will be found.
